newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins fall on Yeltsin operation doubts.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins fall on Yeltsin operation doubts.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell in nervous trading on Monday after a top surgeon said President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery could be delayed up to two months or not take place at all, dealers said.

Renat Akchurin, the doctor chosen to carry out the planned bypass operation on Yeltsin said on Sunday that the 65-year-old leader could wait another 1-1/2 to two months and might have to resign himself to not having it.
"Everything is going down on this news... Even the (investment) funds, known as the least nervous and who have bought MinFins long ago, are selling," Imperial Bank dealer Alexei Denisov said.
Dealers said selling was more active on the Western side, with local operators following the general trend.
They said it was difficult to forecast how long the fall would continue.
"It will all depend on what else they or maybe Yeltsin himself says, if they do after all," one dealer said.
